Seminar Title:

Synergistic Tailoring of Composition-Process-Heat-Treatment in Governing Porosity, Microstructure, Texture, and Mechanical Properties of Al-Cu-Li Alloys

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Metallurgical and Materials Engineering

Speaker Name:

Manojkumar S ( Rollno : 521mm1004)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

M. Tech. Classroom, Annex Building, MM Department

Date and Time:

18 Feb 2026 4:00 PM

Contact:

Kumud Kant Mehta

Abstract:

This research establishes an integrated composition&ndashprocessing&ndashmicrostructure&ndashproperty framework for Al&ndashCu&ndashLi alloys to address the long-standing challenges of limited ductility and porosity in thin-sheet aerospace applications. Two Al&ndashCu&ndashLi alloys, with Cu/Li ratios of ~2 and ~4 and lying within the single-phase FCC field at solution-treatment temperatures, were designed and processed using gravity casting and squeeze casting, followed by severe cold rolling and tailored single- and multi-step solution and aging treatments. Squeeze casting is demonstrated as an enabling route that markedly suppresses porosity, refines microstructure, and allows direct cold rolling to ultra-thin gauges, which is not feasible with gravity-cast material. The Cu/Li ratio and absolute Li content are shown to jointly govern solidification behavior, porosity evolution, deformation texture, recrystallization response, precipitation hierarchy, and tensile properties. Cold rolling produces composition-dependent texture evolution, while annealing control porosity elimination through dissolution of stable phases and formation of metastable Al&ndashCu&ndashLi precipitates. In the heat-treated condition, the Cu/Li~2 alloy developed a high density of T1 (Al₂CuLi) precipitates, achieving maximum strength and suppressing dynamic strain aging, whereas the Li-deficient Cu/Li~4 alloy showed limited precipitation strengthening but enhanced ductility. These results highlight that optimizing the Cu/Li ratio together with tailored heat treatments&mdashsingle-step solution treatment plus double-step aging for strength (Cu/Li~2) and double-step solution treatment plus single-step aging for ductility (Cu/Li~4)&mdashenables the design of Al&ndashCu&ndashLi sheets with application-specific performance for advanced aerospace structures. Comprehensive experimental investigations, supported by advanced microstructural characterization and VPSC-based modeling, establish clear processing&ndashmicrostructure&ndashproperty correlations.
